about: Risk profile R2 (docs/risk-profile/01-plan.md): the validated questionnaires, as published. One source for the phone (asset), the console and the tests. Scoring: 'sum' adds the item values, 'mean' averages them, then 'multiplier' scales the result; a 'reverse' item counts as (max option - value) before that. Bands are inclusive on both ends. A flag fires when one item's value is at least 'min', whatever the total. 'state' is how the result is (ok, warn, bad), never which series it is.

who5_frequency.label: More than half of the time
Less than half of the time

instruments.name: Low mood
instruments.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?

items.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Poor appetite or overeating
Feeling bad about yourself, or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed, or the opposite: being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way

flags.text: You said you have had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself. Please talk about it with someone you trust, or with a doctor.

instruments.source: Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams, J Gen Intern Med 2001. Free to use (Pfizer); bands as published. A screen, not a diagnosis.

instruments.name: Anxiety
instruments.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?

items.text: Feeling nervous, anxious or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Trouble relaxing
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen

instruments.source: Spitzer, Kroenke, Williams & Lowe, Arch Intern Med 2006. Free to use (Pfizer). A screen, not a diagnosis.

instruments.name: Wellbeing

items.text: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits
I have felt calm and relaxed
I have felt active and vigorous
I woke up feeling fresh and rested
My daily life has been filled with things that interest me

bands.label: Low: a PHQ-9 is worth taking

instruments.source: WHO Collaborating Centre in Mental Health (Topp et al., Psychother Psychosom 2015 review). Free to use. 50 or less suggests poor wellbeing, 28 or less likely depression.

instruments.name: Loneliness

items.text: that you lack companionship?
left out?
isolated from others?

instruments.source: Hughes, Waite, Hawkley & Cacioppo, Res Aging 2004 (3-item UCLA scale). 6 or more is the usual cut-off for loneliness (Steptoe et al., PNAS 2013). Loneliness and isolation go with higher mortality (Holt-Lunstad et al. 2015).

instruments.name: Work burnout

items.text: Is your work emotionally exhausting?
Do you feel burnt out because of your work?
Does your work frustrate you?
Do you feel worn out at the end of the working day?
Are you exhausted in the morning at the thought of another day at work?
Do you feel that every working hour is tiring for you?
Do you have enough energy for family and friends during leisure time?

instruments.source: Copenhagen Burnout Inventory, work-related scale (Kristensen et al., Work & Stress 2005). Free to use. 50 or more is the usual cut-off for burnout (Borritz et al. 2006).

instruments.name: Working hours
instruments.prompt: In a usual week, how many hours do you work, paid and unpaid work for your job together?
instruments.source: WHO/ILO joint estimates (Pega et al., Environ Int 2021): 55 hours a week or more goes with a 35 % higher risk of stroke and 17 % higher risk of dying from heart disease than 35-40 hours.
